name: Anamnex
description: Anamnex is a premium-tier memory consolidation pharmaceutical that goes beyond simple short-to-long-term transfer — it actively indexes and organizes consolidated memories for optimal BCI-integrated recall, essentially restructuring recent experience into a searchable, cross-referenced format that interfaces directly with neural implants. Positioned as the executive-class memory tool, it is marketed to Tier 4-5 professionals who cannot afford memory gaps in high-stakes environments.
effects: Deep consolidation of preceding 8-12 hours of experience
BCI-integrated memory indexing for rapid recall
Emotional context preservation with adjustable intensity weighting
Long-term retention rates of 94% at 90 days in clinical trials
side_effects: Requires BCI integration for full effect — limited use without implants
Memory of the consolidation period itself becomes unusually vivid and intrusive
Suppresses natural dream-state memory processing — REM disruption
Rare: memory cross-contamination — adjacent memory traces incorrectly merged
Corporate formulation includes subtle telemetry — memories consolidated under Anamnex are technically logged to Lazarus servers (disclosed in fine print)
duration: Consolidation process: 45-90 minutes. Memory retention: indefinite
cultural_context: Anamnex is a status drug — the price keeps it Spire and upper-Tier 4. Executives take it after critical meetings, negotiations, and briefings. The telemetry clause buried in Lazarus's terms of service is an open secret in GLMZ's privacy activist community — there is a running argument about whether Lazarus has built the world's largest private archive of elite human memory. The Shelf has no access to it, which is precisely the point.
story_hooks: A whistleblower took Anamnex the night they witnessed something they were never supposed to see — meaning Lazarus's servers may hold an indexed copy of their memory of the event

A corporate attorney discovers that a rival's entire deposition strategy was consolidated and BCI-indexed via Anamnex — their opponent will have perfect recall of every word spoken and can query it in real-time during proceedings

Someone hacks the Lazarus memory telemetry archive and discovers it contains indexed recollections from the highest levels of GLMZ's power structure — and is trying to find a buyer before Lazarus finds them
